newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday June 19.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Trade unions started talks with prime minister Romano Prodi about reforms to welfare state but harshly criticize a government reform document. Hard left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti called document, presented as a basis for talks, a "false start" (all).

* The upper house of parliament gave final approval to a so-called "jobs pact" bill on labour market flexibility. The measure, promoted by labour minister Tiziano Treu, is aimed at simplifying procedures to free public expenditure on employment (all).
* Prodi said he had hoped for much more from a European union summit in Amsterdam and described the progress made as too timid (all).

* Roberto Colaninno, managing director of high-tech group Olivetti, said the group's results will make a step towards breakeven this year but a recovery in the information technology sector would not be enough to cover losses elsewhere. Colaninno also said Olivetti would not make a capital increase this year. (all)

* Giovanni Cobolli Gigli, managing director of retailer group Rinascente, said the company's future was based on its alliance with France's Auchan, but the group also had a three-year 1.3 trillion lire investment plan and it aimed to recoup margins and efficiency (all).

* The latest monthly report by Italian Banking Association ABI showed loans and deposits in the banking system rose in May. ABI also forecast Bank of Italy cutting 6.75 percent discount rate to 5.75 percent by the end of 1997 and PSBR for 1997-1998 to be on target for EMU. Forecast economic performance of banking system to deteriorate considerably in 1997-1998 (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
